title: Granular scheduling: latency vs $ scan
content:
Purpose:
Quick oriented notes and text artifacts for an internal one-pager: evaluate how scheduler tick granularity (ms scheduling quantum) impacts p50/p90/p99 latency and $/query across three model families and two client SDK versions. This is a lightweight bench for decisions about changing default scheduling quantum from 8ms -> 4ms -> 1ms.

Summary / thesis (TL;DR):
- Finer scheduling quanta (1ms) reduces tail for short responses at the cost of throughput efficiency; coarse quanta (8ms) is cheaper per-token in sustained throughput but raises p99 for short-turn workloads.
- Break-even depends on workload composition: if >60% requests are <64 tokens, 4ms appears to give best $/p90 tradeoff on our testbed; if workload is heavy long responses (>512 tokens), 8ms retains advantage.
- SDK v2 (non-blocking multiplex) benefits more from fine quanta; SDK v1 (per-connection blocking) suffers fragmentation under 1ms.

Experiment setup (notes, not exhaustive):
- Hardware: 8x A100S (pod-level), single-model per-GPU baseline, small multiplexing overlay in runtime.
- Models: Llama2-7B (float16 baseline), Mistral-7B (float16), RWinf-13B-quant (4-bit quantized).
- Client SDKs: sdk-v1 (blocking, single conn), sdk-v2 (async multiplex).
- Workloads: synthetic mixture to emulate three product profiles:
  - micro-chat: 70% short-turns (avg 24 tokens), 30% medium (avg 128 tokens)
  - editing-burst: 40% short, 40% long (avg 512 tokens), 20% very-long (avg 1024 tokens)
  - qna-snap: 90% short (avg 12 tokens), bursty arrivals (Poisson lambda spike)
- Scheduling quantum set to: 8ms, 4ms, 1ms. Measured for stable-run windows (10m warm, 30m steady) repeated 3x.

Metrics collected (text-table below):
- p50/p90/p99 latencies (ms) per workload mix
- throughput (reqs/s), tokens/sec
- $/q estimated from amortized GPU-second cost + slotization inefficiency (back-of-envelope using internal unit-cost 0.00012 $/gpu-second sample)
- fragmentation ratio = wasted scheduling slots / total slots

Representative results (aggregated median across repeats) - micro-chat workload, sdk-v2:

Quantum | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | reqs/s | tokens/s | $/q (est)
--------|---------|---------|---------|--------|----------|----------
8 ms   | 18      | 42      | 210     | 420    | 100k     | $0.0078
4 ms   | 16      | 34      | 140     | 390    | 92k      | $0.0086
1 ms   | 15      | 28      | 110     | 320    | 80k      | $0.0112

Interpretation (micro-chat / sdk-v2):
- p99 falls ~48% when moving 8ms -> 1ms, p90 ~33% improvement.
- Throughput and tokens/sec drop ~24% between 8ms and 1ms; $/q goes up because idle/wasted tiny-slices increase overhead.
- For latency-sensitive short-turn products, the tail improvement may justify the extra $/q; for cost-sensitive batch embedding-like loads, stick with 8ms.

Representative results (editing-burst workload, sdk-v1):

Quantum | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | reqs/s | tokens/s | $/q (est)
--------|---------|---------|---------|--------|----------|----------
8 ms   | 250     | 640     | 1100    | 85     | 70k      | $0.0214
4 ms   | 240     | 600     | 950     | 78     | 66k      | $0.0229
1 ms   | 230     | 560     | 880     | 64     | 52k      | $0.0287

Interpretation (editing-burst / sdk-v1):
- SDK v1 already shows fragmentation when many long requests multiplex with short ones: 1ms helps tail slightly but throughput penalty is severe.
- Dollar per query increases significantly for this mix at 1ms; long-response heavy products suffer.

ASCII micro-chart: p99 vs quantum (micro-chat, sdk-v2)

p99(ms)
250 |                                                   *
200 |                                *
150 |                   *
100 |         *
 50 | *
     +-----------------------------------------------
       8ms     4ms      1ms
(Note: rough visualization - each * is median p99)

Key diagnostic traces (common patterns observed):
- slot-fragmentation: many 1-8ms holes in GPU scheduler when short-turn bursts interleave with long decodes -> higher overhead for tiny quanta.
- preemption cost: context switch + small kernel re-launch penalty on quantized models ~0.6-1.2ms observed per preempt event.
- SDK interaction: async multiplexing reduces per-req blocking latency but increases concurrency which can make fragmentation worse at very fine quanta unless admission control is tightened.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to repeat with the new kernel-selection patch (runtime PR 402) — quantized model preemption cost may drop and shift break-even point.
- Validate in Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) vs shared-hosted API — tail behavior might differ under multi-tenant noise.
- Produce a product-facing two-slide explainer: one chart p99 vs $/q across quanta for each product persona (micro-chat, editing, qna).
- Quick follow-up experiment: test hybrid policy (4ms default + adaptive collapse to 8ms under sustained long-response mix).

Recommendations (working):
- Short term: do NOT change global default to 1ms. Consider making 4ms the new default for hosted api for customers opting into low-tail plans (beta).
- Medium term: implement adaptive quantum (heuristic: if >30% slots >256 tokens in last-minute window -> raise quantum to 8ms), plus telemetry to measure fragmentation ratio.

Appendix: quick math for $/q estimate (back-of-envelope):
- baseline GPU unit cost used: $0.00012 / gpu-second (internal sample rate)
- effective gpu-second per query = tokens / tokens_per_second + slot-waste_seconds
- slot-waste_seconds approximated from fragmentation ratio * scheduling_quantum * mean_slots_per_query
- these are rough and intended for comparative not absolute accounting.
